title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction: Context (pp. 27-29): Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'magasin', roughly a collection of cells drawn from all admissible subdivisions of a tame/piecewise-linear space. It carries three relations. X ⊴ Y means 'X is a face of Y'. X ∘≪ Y means 'the open cell of X lies in the open cell of Y'; this is the refinement relation between cells of different subdivisions. X ≪ Y means X lies in the closure of Y. A relation |∘| expresses that a figure is a face (vertex-type incidence) of a cell, and || expresses that it meets the closed cell. On p.27 he asks when a subset M' with the induced relations is again a magasin. The key condition is 'Sousmag': if X ∘≪ Y in M' and X' ⊴ X in M', then the lift Y' ⊴ Y of X' (with X' ∘≪ Y') also lies in M'. Ex 1 takes a profigure 𝔏 (its ⊴-closure is a figure, i.e. a subcomplex) and M' = Ouv°(𝔏), the cells whose open cell lies in the open cell of some member of 𝔏. Page 28 proves that Ouv°(𝔏) satisfies Sousmag. (i) Take X, Y, X' ∈ Ouv°(𝔏) with X ∘≪ Y and X' ⊴ X. Then X' ≪ Y ≪ 𝔏̄, so X' ≪ 𝔏̄. Since 𝔏̄ is a figure, there is a unique Z'_0 ∈ 𝔏̄ with X' ∘≪ Z'_0. (ii) X' ∈ Ouv°(𝔏) gives Z'_1 ∈ 𝔏 with X' ∘≪ Z'_1; by uniqueness Z'_1 = Z'_0, so Z'_0 ∈ 𝔏. (iii) Y ∈ Ouv°(𝔏) gives Z ∈ 𝔏 with Y ∘≪ Z. Lifting the face X' successively gives X' ∘≪ Y' ∘≪ Z' with Y' ⊴ Y and Z' ⊴ Z, so Z' ∈ 𝔏̄. By transitivity X' ∘≪ Z', so again Z' = Z'_0 ∈ 𝔏. Hence Y' ∈ Ouv°(Z') ⊂ Ouv°(𝔏), cqfd. Ex 2 asks whether M' = supp°𝔏 (or, nearly equivalently, cosupp°𝔏) is a sub-magasin; these are the cells having the figure as a face, a 'star' of 𝔏. Answer: false in general. Counterexample: take a triangle (a,b,c) and a point d on edge bc, with 𝔏 = {d}. Let Y = (a,b,c), X = (a,b,d) and X' = (b,d). Then X ∘≪ Y and X' ⊴ X; d is a vertex of X and of X', while d only meets the closure of Y. The lift of X' in Y is Y' = (b,c), which contains d in its interior, so d is not a face of Y'. Next page: the fix is to add the condition X ≭ 𝔏, giving the 'multiplicité résiduelle le long de 𝔏', a link-like local structure around a stratum, which is then shown to be a sub-object. Purpose: building local/residual (link, normal) structures of figures inside a combinatorial model of tame topology, presumably for the 'ateliers' of chapter IX.
errors: The step X' ∘≪ Y' ∘≪ Z' ⟹ X' ∘≪ Z' uses transitivity of ∘≪, which is used implicitly (presumably one of the Mag axioms).
The '∈ ?' with 'Ouv°(𝔏)' under Y' marks the goal, not an assertion; the argument itself is complete given the uniqueness of the open lift in a figure.
The remark that supp° and cosupp° are 'pratiquement équivalent[s]' is not justified on the page.
Minor: on line 3 Z'_0 is written once as Z' (notational slip).

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'magasin' of cells across subdivisions with face (⊴) and open-refinement (∘≪) relations, and a notion of sub-magasin (Sousmag condition)
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial models of tame/PL stratified spaces; posets of cells under subdivision; o-minimal cell decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme (Grothendieck's Esquisse); o-minimal structures (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight); PL topology (Rourke–Sanderson)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of tame topology appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific axiomatics appears unpublished

ideas.what: Open star Ouv°(𝔏) of a profigure is closed under lifting of faces (proof via uniqueness of the open cell of a figure containing a given cell)
ideas.modern_name: Open star of a subcomplex is compatible with subdivision

ideas.what: Counterexample: the set of cells having a point-figure as a face is not stable under subdivision lifting (d on edge bc)
ideas.modern_name: Stars are not subdivision-invariant; need for links/residual structures

missed.claim: This page belongs to an unpublished axiomatization ('magasins', 'multiplicités', 'figures', 'profigures') of a combinatorial tame topology. The page itself is routine verification, but the framework as a whole is not in the literature.
missed.quote: Alors M' = Ouv°(𝔏) est un sous-magasin, i.e. satisfait Sousmag.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with o-minimal and exit-path/stratified-space formalisms; of documentary interest rather than as a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct but routine verification and a simple PL counterexample inside an unpublished framework; the framework is of interest, but nothing on this page is a striking result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: the image reads '∃! Z'_0 ∈ 𝔏̄ avec X' ∘≪ Z'' (Z' without subscript at the end; the subscript 0 is intended).
Ex 2: 'Est-ce un sous-ens. ouvert[?]' is more likely 'Est-ce un sous-magasin ?', given the context of sub-magasins.
'(union supports contractibles[?]' is uncertain; the handwriting suggests '(mais supposons ... contractible)' or similar — illegible, should be marked [?].
The struck-out fragment after 'cosupp° 𝔏' reads roughly '(du moins, bien...' and is struck through, which is correctly marked.
